bib.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning

question: Can FlashAttention be made much closer to GEMM efficiency by better work partitioning across thread blocks and warps?
hypothesis: FlashAttention's inefficiency comes from suboptimal work partitioning between thread blocks and warps, causing low occupancy or unnecessary shared memory reads/writes.
contributions: Tweak the algorithm to reduce non-matmul FLOPs
Parallelize forward and backward over sequence length in addition to batch and heads
Partition work between warps inside a thread block to avoid split-K and reduce shared memory traffic

method.summary: Exact attention kernel (CUTLASS 3.x based) that keeps an un-scaled output accumulator, stores only logsumexp, swaps loop order so row blocks are parallel across thread blocks, and splits Q across warps instead of K/V. Benchmarked on A100 and H100 and in end-to-end GPT training.
method.task: GPU attention kernel (forward and backward) speed

other.block_sizes: {64, 128} x {64, 128}, tuned manually per head dimension

parameters.tokens_per_batch: batch size set so total tokens is 16k

other.fwd_flops_formula: 4 * seqlen^2 * head dimension * number of heads, halved with causal mask
other.e2e_flops_formula: 6 * seqlen * number of params + 12 * number of layers * hidden dim * seqlen^2 (attention term not halved for causal)

metrics.name: Speed
metrics.definition: attention FLOPs by the formula divided by runtime

metrics.name: End-to-end training throughput
metrics.definition: model FLOPs by Megatron-LM formula divided by time, per GPU

eval.protocol: Single runs reported as bar values; no seeds, repeats or variance stated.

results.claim: FlashAttention-2 reaches up to 225 TFLOPs/s per A100 in end-to-end GPT training, 72% model FLOPs utilization.
results.setup: GPT3-2.7B, 8k context, 8xA100 80GB SXM; FLOPs via Megatron formula without halving attention term
results.quote: reaching up to 225 TFLOPs/s per A100 GPU
results.table: Table 1, row GPT3-2.7B 8k context, column FlashAttention-2

results.claim: End-to-end speedup is 2.8x over no FlashAttention and 1.3x over FlashAttention.
results.setup: GPT-style 1.3B and 2.7B, 2k or 8k context, 8xA100; best case
results.quote: FlashAttention-2 yields 2.8× speedup compared to a baseline without FlashAttention
results.note: Text says '1.3× speedup compared to FlashAttention-2' in Sec 4.2, apparently a typo for FlashAttention.

results.claim: Attention kernel reaches up to 230 TFLOPs/s, 73% of A100 theoretical max.
results.setup: A100 80GB SXM4, forward, no causal mask, head dim 128 (Fig 5b shows 227 at 2k)
results.quote: FlashAttention-2 reaches up to 230 TFLOPs/s, 73% of the theoretical maximum TFLOPs/s on A100 GPUs.

results.claim: FlashAttention-2 is about 2x faster than FlashAttention, 1.7-3.0x in range.
results.setup: A100 attention benchmark, seq 512 to 16k, head dim 64/128, with and without causal mask
results.note: Sec 3 intro says 2-3x; abstract says around 2x.

results.claim: Backward pass reaches up to 63% of theoretical max throughput.
results.quote: up to 63% of the theoretical max throughput in the backward pass

results.claim: FlashAttention (v1) reaches only 30-50% of peak in forward and 25-35% in backward on A100.
results.quote: the forward pass only reaches 30-50% of the theoretical maximum FLOPs/s of the device
results.note: Abstract says 25-40% for FlashAttention without splitting forward/backward.

results.claim: Each non-matmul FLOP is 16x more expensive than a matmul FLOP on A100.
results.source: A100 specs (312 TFLOPs/s FP16/BF16 matmul vs 19.5 non-matmul FP32)
results.quote: each non-matmul FLOP is 16× more expensive than a matmul FLOP

results.claim: Skipping fully masked blocks makes causal attention 1.7-1.8x faster than without a mask.
results.setup: large sequence lengths, about half of blocks skipped
results.quote: This leads to around 1.7-1.8× speedup compared to attention without the causal mask.

results.claim: Same code on H100 with no Hopper-specific instructions reaches up to 335 TFLOPs/s.
results.setup: H100 80GB SXM5, forward+backward, no causal mask, head dim 128

results.claim: FlashAttention-2 is up to 10x faster than PyTorch standard attention.
results.quote: FlashAttention-2 can be up to 10× faster.
results.note: Quote text reads 'Compared to a standard attention implementation in PyTorch, FlashAttention-2 can be up to 10× faster'.

limits: Block sizes tuned manually per head dimension; auto-tuning left to future work.
H100 results use no TMA or 4th-gen Tensor Core instructions; authors expect another 1.5-2x from them.
Single-run bars, no variance; training-speed numbers only for 1.3B/2.7B GPT-style models, no model quality results.
End-to-end FLOPs formula does not halve attention FLOPs for causal masking, which inflates reported utilization relative to a halved count.
No FP8, AMD, or inference/decode benchmark.

terms.definition: FlashAttention scheme splitting K and V across warps while Q is shared, requiring shared-memory reduction

lineage.work: FlashAttention: Fast and memory-efficient exact attention with IO-awareness

lineage.note: Loop swap and sequence-length parallelism first suggested and implemented there
